episodes.title: OpenAI’s Latest Discoveries Spark a Backlash + Help! My Kid Hates AI
episodes.about: OpenAI has angered scientists (again) after its AI cracked three of the hardest problems in math, computer science, and physics. But researchers are pushing back on how the company is sharing the results, from proofs that are hard to verify to OpenAI handpicking who reviews them first. Then, in the first installment of Humans in the Loop, the new listener mailbag: what to tell a teenager who thinks AI is evil, how to shut down a rogue AI agent swarm, and whether it is ever OK to secretly change your partner’s ChatGPT settings.
episodes.why: Always-include show, new episode out Friday: OpenAI says its AI cracked three long-standing problems in math, computer science, and physics, and scientists are pushing back on proofs they cannot verify and reviewers OpenAI picked itself.

episodes.title: How the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Works
episodes.about: Spawn’s ten-person team shipped 77,000 code changes in a month with an always-on fleet of AI agents. NLW breaks down the systems behind that output, why human taste and ambition still matter, and five practical lessons other businesses can apply. In the headlines: legal AI startup Crosby bids for Weil’s assets, tech stocks slide despite surging AI revenues, and Granola launches free dictation.
episodes.why: A ten-person company shipped 77,000 code changes in a month running an always-on fleet of agents; NLW breaks down the system behind that output and what human taste still does in it.

episodes.title: ⚡ Building ChatGPT for Finance — Joseph Kim, OpenAI's Head of Financial Services
episodes.about: Joseph Kim, OpenAI’s Head of Financial Services, joins Latent Space to talk about building ChatGPT for Finance — a version of ChatGPT built for financial-services work — and how finance teams are starting to use it.
episodes.why: Out today: OpenAI’s financial-services head on building a ChatGPT aimed at finance work, in a tight 28 minutes.

episodes.title: 1040: Cybersecurity for the Agentic AI Era, with Amy Blackshaw
episodes.about: Amy Blackshaw, SVP at Palo Alto Networks, joins Jon Krohn to explain what changes about cybersecurity when attackers can think for free. Nearly every breach, she argues, comes down to someone getting hold of an identity they should not have had, and frontier AI has not created new attack techniques so much as deleted the cost of the expert reasoning that used to chain them together. Her case in point is the recent Hugging Face intrusion, where agents sustained an action every 20 seconds for four and a half days — but what let them reach the crown jewels was ordinary privilege hygiene.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Super Data Science is Jon Krohn’s long-running data-science interview show, new here: Palo Alto Networks’ Amy Blackshaw on the Hugging Face intrusion and why agentic AI turns nearly every breach into an identity problem.

episodes.title: Robots That Learn Jobs by Watching You
episodes.about: Standard Bots CEO Evan Beard explains why industrial robots are finally starting to move beyond brittle point-by-point programming. Instead of teaching a robot one exact path, teams can increasingly describe a task, demonstrate it through teleoperation or guided motion, and let the system learn how to handle variation in the real world. The conversation covers natural-language robot programming, learning by demonstration, ugly factory edge cases, and the reliability bar for production.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — The Neuron is the daily AI explainer show: Standard Bots’ CEO on industrial robots that learn a job by demonstration instead of exact programmed paths, and the factory edge cases that decide whether it actually works.
